*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the
social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of June
22, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically
  for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should
  indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close
  of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office
  of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

2. By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can
participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l  The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5
  minutes prior.
  l  If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline
  phones are highly recommended.
  l  If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it is
  requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission.
  Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.
  l  Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed below for the
  respective City Council Dates:
  l  June 8, 2021 – Access Code: 5362462# wait two seconds and press # again
   l  If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it is
  requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission.
  Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.
  l  Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed below for the
  respective City Council Dates:
  l  June 8, 2021 – Access Code: 5362462# wait two seconds and press # again
  l  June 15, 2021 – Access Code: 4755419# wait two seconds and press # again
  l  June 22, 2021 – Access Code: 4500707# wait two seconds and press # again
  l  June 29, 2021 – Access Code: 4731505# wait two seconds and press # again

  3.Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for
  details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting; however,
members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2
noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate alternative
formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42
U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who
requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or offer
public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of
the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor,
Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and
aallen@cityofinglewood.orgno later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  June 22, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  June 22, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:02 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas other than the public hearing.
  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Citywide Parking Permits, specifically
  regarding the City requiring $100 for additional parking permits.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos.
  SPH-1, Setting Public Hearing to place delinquent charges for sewer and refuse
  collection services on Tax Rolls, and 3, Approval of the Minutes of the Meetings held on
  December 15, 2020, and January 12, 2021. She also spoke on Brown Act Violations,
  specifically the time limits allowed to speak on Agenda Items.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June
  18, 2021, in the amount of $5,065,088.26 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on December 8,
  2020, and the Special Meeting held on December 8, 2020, be approved. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and

  1
   June 22, 2021

  Abstain: Council Member Faulk.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on December 15,
  2020, and January 12, 2021, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claim filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1. Yolanda Dominguez for alleged personal injury; slip and fall on March 5, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby reject the claim listed as A-1. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT NO. 5 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-201 APPROVED – COUNTY OF
  LOS ANGELES WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY
  SERVICES. Staff report dated June 22, 2021, was presented recommending approval of
  Amendment Five of the Elderly Nutrition Program Services Subaward Number
  ENP202107 with County of Los Angeles Workforce Development Aging and
  Community Services (WDACS) to reallocate baseline grant funding for provision of the
  Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 5 to Agreement No. 20-201
  in the amount of $104,197. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT NO. 6 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-201 APPROVED – COUNTY OF
  LOS ANGELES WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY
  SERVICES; RESOLUTION NO. 21-95 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET; RESOLUTION NO. 21-96 ADOPTED – GRANTING
  MAYOR BUTTS AUTHORIZATION TO SIGN CERTAIN DOCUMENTS
  RELATED TO THE ELDERLY NUTRITION PROGRAM. Staff report dated June
  22, 2021, was presented recommending approval of Amendment Six of the Elderly
  Nutrition Program Services Subaward Number ENP202107 with County of Los Angeles
  Workforce Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to reallocate
  baseline grant funding for provision of the Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 6 to Agreement No. 20-
  201 in the amount of $435,500; 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-95 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2020-2021ANNUAL BUDGET AND
  TO COMMIT CERTAIN FUTURE GRANT FUNDS TO FISCAL YEAR
  2021-22

  and; 3) Adopt Resolution No. 21-96 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD GRANTING THE MAYOR THE AUTHORITY TO
  SIGN CERTAIN DOCUMENTS RELATED TO THE ELDERLY
  NUTRITION PROGRAM SUBAWARD AGREEMENT THROUGH
  AND INCLUDING JUNE 30, 2022, WITHOUT THE NEED OF
  BRINGING SAID DOCUMENTS TO THE CITY COUNCIL

  2
   June 22, 2021

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-224 APPROVED – URBAN
  TRANS CONSULTANTS, INC. Staff report dated June 22, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 19-224 with
  UrbanTrans Consultants, Inc., extending the term of the agreement by one year to further
  aid with the operation, management, and future funding securement of the Transportation
  Demand Management Pilot Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 19-224 in an
  amount not to exceed $369,527. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  RESOLUTION NO. 21-97 ADOPTED – PUBLIC HEARING SET TO DECLARE
  INTENTION TO ADOPT THE PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR REPORT
  CONCERNING SEWER AND REFUSE COLLECTION SERVICES;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-98 ADOPTED – ELECTING TO PLACE DELINQUENT
  SEWER SERVICE FEES ON THE TAX ROLLS; RESOLUTION NO. 21-99
  ADOPTED – ELECTING TO PLACE DELINQUENT SEWER SERVICE FEES
  ON THE TAX ROLLS. Staff report dated June 22, 2021, was presented recommending
  adoption of a resolution declaring the City’s intention to adopt the report of the Public
  Works Director concerning delinquent charges for sewer and refuse collection services
  (Health and Safety Code Sections 5470, et seq.), and requesting that a public hearing be
  set for any protest.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 21-97 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFNORIA DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO
  ADOPT THE REPORT OF THE PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR
  CONCERNING DELINQUENT CHARGES FOR SEWER AND
  REFUSE COLLECTION SERVICES (HEALTH AND SAFETY CODE
  SECTIONS 5470, EST SEQ.) AND TO SET A PUBLIC HEARING FOR
  ANY PROTEST ON JULY 20, 2021

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None;

  2) Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for July 20, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.;

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby: 3) Adopt Resolution No. 21-98 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, ELECTING TO PLACE DELINQUENT
  SEWER SERVICE FEES ON THE TAX ROLLS PURSUANT TO
  DIVISION 5, PART 3, CHAPTER 6 OF THE HEALTH AND SAFETY
  CODE OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA (COMMENCING WITH
  ARTICLE 4, SECTIONS 5470, ET SEQ.)

  and; 4) Adopt Resolution No. 21-99 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA ELECTING TO PLACE DELINQUENT

  3
   June 22, 2021

  REFUSE COLLECTION CHARGES ON THE TAX ROLLS
  PURSUANT TO DIVISION 5, PART 3, CHAPTER 6 OF THE HEALTH
  AND SAFETY CODE OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  (COMMENCING WITH ARTICLE 4, SECTIONS 5470, ET SEQ.)

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PUBLIC HEARING SET – AMENDING INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE
  CHAPTERS 10 (PUBLIC WORKS) AND 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING). Staff
  report dated June 22, 2021, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to
  consider an ordinance to amend Inglewood Municipal Code Chapters 10 (Public Works)
  and 12 (Planning and Zoning) including Zoning Code Amendment (ZCA-2021-002) to
  modify signage regulations for Banners in the Public Right of Way, citywide.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for July 20, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding problems with the audio while calling into
  Council Meetings. She also spoke on continuous and ongoing Brown Act Violations, and
  questioned when were the Police Oversight Commission meetings held. Additionally, she
  requested a meeting with Council and Chief Fronterotta.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Youth Skill Center opening, the Police BMW
  Motorcycle, and the Parking Permits.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported her
  anticipation of attending the Summer Bash event along with her team at SoFi Stadium.
  While in attendance, they will have the opportunity to sign voters up to register and
  update registration cards. Additionally, she expressed her excitement to meet and service
  Inglewood residents.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:44 p.m.

  Approved this 28th day of September, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
